In the course of many opposition demonstrations, all three applicants were arrested and convicted.
The first applicant alleged that between approximately 10 a.m. and 11 a.m. on 31 March 2011, after he had taken his child to kindergarten, police officers stopped his car.
The first applicant alleged that police officers requested that he follow them to a police station after stopping his car on 31 March 2011.
The first applicant did not oppose the police officers' demand and was taken to police station no. 20 of the Nasimi District Police Office.
At an unspecified time on 31 March 2011, the first applicant was informed that he was being detained in connection with the upcoming demonstration of 2 April 2011.
At around 2 p.m. on 31 March 2011, the first applicant learned that he would not be released from detention.
According to the official records, the first applicant was arrested for disobeying a lawful order of a police officer.
According to the first applicant, he was not given access to a lawyer after his arrest or while in police custody.
The second applicant alleged that at around 10.30 a.m. on 31 March 2011, when he was still in bed, three police officers entered his apartment without an arrest warrant.
The second applicant's father let the police officers into the apartment on 31 March 2011.
The police officers took the second applicant to police station no. 3 of the Sumgait City Police Office on 31 March 2011.
At an unspecified time on 31 March 2011, the second applicant was questioned about his political activities at police station no. 3 of the Sumgait City Police Office.
According to the official records, the second applicant was arrested for minor hooliganism.
According to the official records, the second applicant was arrested for disobeying a lawful order of a police officer.
On the day of the arrest, an administrative-offence report was issued by police officer E.S. in respect of the second applicant.

The administrative-offence report issued by police officer E.S. stated that the second applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 296 (minor hooliganism) of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The administrative-offence report issued by police officer E.S. stated that the second applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The second applicant refused to sign the administrative-offence report.
According to the second applicant, he was never provided with a copy of the administrative-offence report or with other documents in his case file.
According to the second applicant, he was not given access to a lawyer after his arrest or while he was kept in police custody.
According to the third applicant, at around 11 a.m. on 31 March 2011 he went with his lawyer to the Sumgait City Police Office.

The third applicant alleged that when he had been outside the Sumgait City Police Office and no longer accompanied by his lawyer, police officers arrested him without explaining the reasons for doing so.
The third applicant alleged that police officers took him to police station no. 4 of the Sumgait City Police Office after arresting him on 31 March 2011.
According to the official records, the third applicant was arrested for minor hooliganism.

The administrative-offence report issued by police officer V.J. stated that the third applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 296 (minor hooliganism) of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The third applicant refused to sign the administrative-offence report.
According to the third applicant, he was never provided with a copy of the administrative-offence report or with other documents in his case file.
According to the third applicant, he was not given access to a lawyer after his arrest or while he was kept in police custody.
According to the third applicant, he was not given an opportunity to hire a lawyer of his own choice to represent him at the hearing before the Sumgait City Court, which began at 4 p.m.
The third applicant asked the judge to postpone the examination of the case for one hour so that his lawyer could arrive at the court.
The judge decided to adjourn the hearing for only thirty minutes and to recommence the hearing at 4.30 p.m., which was not enough time for the third applicant's lawyer to arrive.
According to the transcript of the court hearing before the Sumgait City Court, the third applicant refused the assistance of a State-funded lawyer.

Article 49 of the 1995 Constitution of Azerbaijan provides that everyone has the right, having notified the respective governmental bodies in advance, to assemble with other people peacefully and without arms, to organise meetings, demonstrations, protests and marches, and to stage pickets.

Under Article 5 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, advance written notification is required in order to agree on the place and time of an assembly and the route of a march, with the purpose of enabling the relevant local executive authority to take necessary measures.
Under Article 5 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, the notification has to be done in writing five days before the demonstration.

Article 8 §§ IV and V of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with broad powers to issue relevant orders so as to prohibit a public assembly.
Article 8 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with broad powers to issue relevant orders so as to stop a public assembly.

Article 9 §§ II and VII of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with broad powers to restrict or change the place, route and/or time of a public assembly.
Article 9 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with broad powers to designate specific areas for public assemblies.

At the material time, Article 375.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that a defender and a representative shall be allowed to participate in administrative-offence proceedings from the time an administrative-offence report is drawn up.

At the material time, Article 375.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that if an individual is subjected to an administrative arrest for committing an administrative offence, a defender shall be allowed to participate in the administrative-offence proceedings from the moment of the administrative arrest.

At the material time, Article 376.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that if it is impossible for the lawyer chosen by the person against whom administrative-offence proceedings are being carried out to attend, a judge shall appoint a lawyer for that person in accordance with the legislation of the Republic of Azerbaijan.

At the material time, Article 376.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that if a person subjected to an administrative arrest has no possibility to hire a lawyer due to his or her financial situation, his or her legal assistance shall be funded by the State, and in this case a lawyer may not refuse to carry out his or her duties.

At the material time, Article 396.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that an authorised official may use administrative arrest as a measure to prevent administrative offences, to establish the identity of a person, to draw up an administrative-offence report if this cannot be done at the place of the administrative offence and if the drawing up of a report is important, to ensure the correct and timely examination of administrative-offence cases, and to ensure the implementation of decisions in administrative-offence cases.

At the material time, Article 398.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that administrative arrest, that is the short-term restriction of an individual's liberty, may be applied in exceptional circumstances when deemed necessary for ensuring the correct and timely examination of an administrative-offence case or for the implementation of a decision in an administrative-offence case, except for instances set out in legislation.

At the material time, Article 410.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that an individual who is subject to administrative-offence proceedings or a representative of a legal entity shall be given an opportunity to familiarise himself with the administrative-offence report.

At the material time, Article 410.4 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that an individual who is subject to the administrative-offence proceedings or a representative of a legal entity has the right to a copy of the administrative-offence report.

At the material time, Article 414.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that a report concerning an administrative offence punishable by administrative detention shall be sent to a judge for examination immediately after it has been drawn up.

At the material time, Article 422.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that cases concerning an administrative offence punishable by administrative detention shall be examined on the day of receipt by the court of an administrative-offence report.

At the material time, Article 422.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that cases against persons subjected to administrative arrest shall be examined at the latest within 48 hours of their arrest.
Under Article 368 of the Code of Administrative Offences, a public prosecutor has the right to participate in administrative proceedings.
Chapter 28 of the Code of Administrative Offences enumerates the participants of administrative proceedings and their rights and obligations.

Chapter 28 of the Code of Administrative Offences does not mention the prosecution — a police officer, public prosecutor or any other public official representing the prosecution — as a participant of the proceedings.
